notes: Strengths: The original agent's architectural approach was correct—a 4-module daemon (writer, reader, watcher, uploader) with orchestration directly addresses bidirectional Supernote sync. All major components have implementations: RATTA_RLE encoder/decoder, PIL rendering, Claude vision integration, FSEvents monitoring, Playwright upload flow. Test coverage exists across modules. Weaknesses: Execution quality was poor. The codebase left bugs unfixed: broken __init__.py imports, main.py missing awaits and wrong dict keys, misconfigured pyproject.toml, mismatched test assertions. Agent killed 3 times by zero-output detector, indicating inefficient execution path. Work required separate verification pass to achieve passing tests. Efficiency: Multiple respawns show inefficient approach; agent didn't validate end-to-end integration. Downstream Impact: Work required immediate external fixes to be usable. Verdict: Meets Expectations. Agent tackled the right problem with sound architecture but delivered incomplete, buggy code. FLIP 0.28 was justified. Approach was salvageable but execution discipline was poor.
